speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned having a psychiatric condition and a new movement disorder; can you tell me specifically what symptoms you are experiencing and for how long?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is excellent news regarding your psychiatric symptoms. However, I notice you have a new movement disorder; have you developed any stiffness in your limbs, tremors, or a feeling of being "stuck" in a position since starting the risperidone?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; those symptoms strongly suggest akathisia. Did this restlessness begin shortly after you started the risperidone, and have you noticed any involuntary muscle contractions or jaw clenching as well? REQUEST TEST: Extrapyramidal_Symptom_Assessment.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Normal Extrapyramidal Symptom Assessment Scale (SAS) score consistent with subjective report of akathisia; no objective parkinsonism, dystonia, or tardive dyskinesia observed on examination.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Risperidone-induced akathisia.

The subjective symptoms of inner restlessness, pacing, and leg crossing are classic for this condition. Given that the Extrapyramidal Symptom Assessment Scale did not detect objective parkinsonism, dystonia, or tardive dyskinesia, the clinical picture strongly points to akathisia rather than other movement disorders. We can proceed with adjusting your antipsychotic regimen or adding a beta-blocker to manage this side effect.
